title: Dominic and the Hollow
premise: Lior Eastwick, last apprentice of the Hollow Guild, survives in the city of Vess by selling charms too weak to be called magic — until the old gods, long silent since the Purge, begin answering prayers again, and every answered prayer burns a hole in the world. Hunted by the Inquisitor Sarel Vane and bound to a fading god who speaks through her dead master's voice, Lior must gather the scattered members of her dying guild to reopen the Door their founders once sealed. The price of survival, she learns, is that someone must stay behind to hold it open — and justice outside the law means deciding for herself who pays. In the end, Lior chooses not to escape alone: she gives the guild's inheritance back to the god, unmaking Vess's magic ban at the cost of her own power, and walks out of a country that no longer exists carrying nothing but its name.
about_author: Orsen Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about institutions, grief, and the small mercies people invent when the law offers none.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Lior sells luck-knots and fever-wards in Vess's night market, hiding her guild sigil beneath her sleeve. A desperate mother buys a charm that shouldn't work — and does. POV: Lior. Beat: quiet dread as the impossible happens in her own hands.

chapters.title: The Law of Ash
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sarel Vane tours the market, burning confiscated charms and questioning sellers. Lior watches her master's old tools go up in flame. POV: Lior. Beat: fear sharpened into resentment; the law is personal now.

chapters.title: What the Mother Prayed For
chapters.summary: The mother returns: her son's fever broke, but he wakes speaking a language no one knows. Lior recognizes it as Old Hollowtongue — the guild's liturgical tongue. POV: Lior. Beat: guilt curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Voices in the Sealed Room
chapters.summary: Lior breaks into the abandoned guildhall and hears her dead master Aldous answering from behind the sealed inner door. He tells her the gods are waking and the Door must be found. POV: Lior. Beat: terror and longing entwined.

chapters.title: Sarel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sarel investigates the healed boy, tracing the prayer to the night market. Her own faith in the Purge wavers as she reads confiscated records of what the gods were. POV: Sarel. Beat: doubt planted in the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Guild That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lior seeks Tessin, a former guildsman turned licensed apothecary who denies everything. He slips her a map fragment anyway — the first piece of the Door. POV: Lior. Beat: betrayal softened by reluctant loyalty.

chapters.title: Prayer Burns
chapters.summary: Across Vess, answered prayers leave scorched hollows in walls and streets. The city blames smugglers; Lior knows better. She feels each burn like a hook behind her ribs. POV: Lior. Beat: the stakes become physical and spreading.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Speaks Hollowtongue
chapters.summary: Lior visits the healed child, Wren, who recites guild oaths he never learned. Through him, Aldous warns: the god waking under Vess is hungry and half-mad. POV: alternating Lior/Wren. Beat: innocence weaponized; dread deepens.

chapters.title: A Warrant with Her Name
chapters.summary: Sarel raids the night market with a sketch of Lior. Tessin burns his own shop to cover her escape, staying behind to be arrested. POV: Lior. Beat: the price of survival made concrete — someone always pays.

chapters.title: Road Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Fleeing east, Lior learns the border provinces were dissolved years ago; maps show nothing where the Door should be. She travels through villages that worship in secret. POV: Lior. Beat: isolation and resolve.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Lior finds Ivet, an exiled cartographer who maps places erased from record. He confirms the Door lies in a village that officially never existed. POV: Ivet. Beat: wonder amid ruin; a new ally with his own guilt.

chapters.title: Sarel Interrogates Tessin
chapters.summary: Tessin gives Sarel nothing but a question: what did the Purge actually save anyone from? Sarel opens a sealed archive against orders. POV: Sarel. Beat: the antagonist crosses her own line.

chapters.title: What the Archive Said
chapters.summary: Sarel discovers the Purge didn't kill the gods — the guild sealed them, and the Inquisition has been guarding a prison, not a victory. POV: Sarel. Beat: worldview inversion; she begins hunting the truth instead of witches.

chapters.title: Hollowtongue Rising
chapters.summary: Wren escapes custody, drawn toward Lior by the voice in him. Sarel follows the same trail. Two hunters converge on one fugitive child. POV: Sarel then Wren. Beat: chase tension; the child as compass.

chapters.title: The Village Unwritten
chapters.summary: Lior and Ivet reach Errow, a town off every map where old rites persist openly. Its priestess recognizes Lior's sigil and calls her 'heir.' POV: Lior. Beat: belonging offered at a cost she can't yet see.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Well
chapters.summary: Wren arrives in Errow, pursued by Sarel. The priestess shields them; Sarel arrives and, seeing the rites, hesitates rather than arrests. POV: Lior. Beat: enemies forced into uneasy truce by shared revelation.

chapters.title: The First Key Is a Confession
chapters.summary: The priestess explains the Door needs three keys held by surviving guild members. The first is held by Maren Cole — who bought her freedom by informing on the guild during the Purge. POV: Lior. Beat: justice versus mercy framed.

chapters.title: Maren Cole's Debt
chapters.summary: Lior confronts Maren, now wealthy and terrified. Maren surrenders her key only after confessing which names she sold — including Aldous's. POV: Lior. Beat: rage, then cold clarity about what justice outside the law means.

chapters.title: Sarel's Report, Unsent
chapters.summary: Sarel writes the truth for her superiors and realizes it will be buried — or get her burned alongside the guild. She pockets the report. POV: Sarel. Beat: the antagonist becomes a defector in secret.

chapters.title: The Second Key Is Buried
chapters.summary: The second key belonged to a guildsman executed in the Purge; it was buried with him in the Inquisition's mass grave outside Vess. POV: Lior. Beat: grim determination; they must return to the lion's den.

chapters.title: Back Through the Gates
chapters.summary: Disguised as pilgrims, Lior, Ivet, and Wren enter Vess under curfew. The city's prayer-burns have spread; panic rules the streets. POV: Lior. Beat: homecoming as infiltration; dread at every checkpoint.

chapters.title: Graveyard of the Convicted
chapters.summary: Digging in the convict graves, they find the key — and hundreds of small charms buried with the dead, still warm. The god under Vess stirs at the disturbance. POV: Ivet. Beat: sacrilege and sorrow; the dead are witnesses.

chapters.title: Aldous Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Through Wren, Aldous admits the guild didn't seal the gods to protect the world — they sealed them to seize magic for themselves, and failed. POV: Lior. Beat: inheritance revealed as theft; grief for a false idol.

chapters.title: Sarel Catches Them
chapters.summary: Sarel corners the group at the graveyard wall — and lets them go, demanding only the truth in writing. She gives them her badge as a pass through the gates. POV: Sarel. Beat: trust extended across enemy lines; point of no return.

chapters.title: Riots of the Answered
chapters.summary: Vess erupts as more prayers are answered; the poor storm the temples demanding their god back. The Inquisition declares martial law. POV: Sarel. Beat: chaos as consequence; the old order cracking.

chapters.title: The Third Key Refuses
chapters.summary: The third key is held by the guild's last elder, Ossa, who lives hidden inside the Inquisition itself as a cleanser of archives. She refuses: opening the Door freed nothing, it only moves the hunger elsewhere. POV: Ossa. Beat: the plan challenged on moral grounds.

chapters.title: What the Door Actually Opens
chapters.summary: Ossa reveals the truth: the Door doesn't release the gods — it feeds them. Someone must remain on the far side, willingly, as the guild's heir. That was Aldous's role; he died before taking it. POV: Lior. Beat: the full weight of inheritance lands.

chapters.title: Lior's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lior agrees to go — if the god answers the prayers of Vess's poor justly, not hungrily, and if the magic ban ends. Ossa accepts on the god's behalf. POV: Lior. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely; justice negotiated outside any law.

chapters.title: Sarel Reads the Truth Aloud
chapters.summary: Sarel publicly reads the archive's account of the Purge from the temple steps, shattering the Inquisition's legitimacy. She is arrested by her own order. POV: Sarel. Beat: costly courage; the antagonist completes her turn.

chapters.title: Breaking Sarel Out
chapters.summary: Lior uses the guild's last real magic — the kind she swore off — to free Sarel from the cells. Using it costs her memories of her childhood. POV: Lior. Beat: the price of survival paid in self; bond forged between former enemies.

chapters.title: March to Errow
chapters.summary: The company — Lior, Ivet, Wren, Ossa, freed Sarel — travels to Errow as refugees and pilgrims swell the roads behind them, following rumor of the Door. POV: rotating. Beat: momentum and dread; a nation walking toward its own threshold.

chapters.title: The Priestess's Warning
chapters.summary: The priestess reveals the god has been whispering to Errow too, promising miracles for obedience. Half the village wants the Door opened; half wants it destroyed forever. POV: Lior. Beat: allies fracture; mob logic vs. covenant.

chapters.title: Night of Split Banners
chapters.summary: Errow's factions clash at the well. Wren, channeling the god, nearly drowns in the crowd's fervor until Lior sings the guild's binding hymn. POV: Wren. Beat: near-tragedy; the child saved by inherited song.

chapters.title: Three Keys, One Hand
chapters.summary: At the sealed door beneath Errow's chapel, the keys are joined. The Door opens onto a country that no longer exists — a hollow echo of Vess, beautiful and starving. POV: Lior. Beat: awe and horror; the threshold crossed.

chapters.title: The God's True Face
chapters.summary: Inside, the god appears as everyone Lior has lost, including Aldous. It offers her anything — her memories back, her master alive — to make the staying easy. POV: Lior. Beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: Sarel's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Sarel argues she should stay: her whole life built the prison; her penance should hold the door. Lior refuses — the debt is the guild's, and she is its heir. POV: Sarel. Beat: grace contested; both women transformed.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Given Back
chapters.summary: Instead of staying bodily, Lior dissolves the guild's hoarded power — her inheritance — into the god, sating its hunger and ending the need for a keeper. The ban on magic dies with the guild. POV: Lior. Beat: climax resolved by renunciation, not force.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: The hollow country fades as the god, fed by returned inheritance rather than stolen prayer, releases it. The company walks out into ordinary dawn over Errow. POV: Ivet. Beat: exhaustion, release, quiet grief for what was given up.

chapters.title: After the Ban
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Vess rebuilds without the Inquisition; Sarel testifies before a citizen council; charms are sold openly. Lior, powerless but remembered by the god, teaches children the guild's songs as history, not spellcraft. POV: Lior. Beat: bittersweet ordinariness.

chapters.title: The Name We Carried Out
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, Lior visits the unmarked grave of the Purge dead. A single prayer she whispers is answered — gently, once. Some inheritances survive even their owners. POV: Lior. Beat: closure; the theme resolved in a whisper.
